base.title: Add real-Rust web demo with visible climate evidence and reference crop options
base.body:
Combines the Flutter Milestone 4C integration, NASA POWER backend and Rust v0.2 branches with the preserved Android tooling fixes, and adds a Flutter web demo that can run locally or on the local Wi-Fi network.

Browser analysis calls a separate Python service using the actual compiled Rust executable. Android retains its on-device FRB path and existing request behavior; Rust integration and v0.2 APIs are unchanged. Live NASA, captured real NASA replay and explicit synthetic fixture presentation remain distinct, with no automatic substitution on failure.

The results screen now displays rainfall/temperature totals, monthly values and daily coverage, field inputs, source provenance and missing evidence. Live web mode defaults to the last completed calendar year. Rice fields include a baseline and two published rice–pulse reference options assessed by Rust. Sources remain reference-only and suitability remains unknown; no ranking, yield, profit or planting-date claims are introduced. Other crops get an explicit unavailable-recommendation state. Unknown dates no longer produce an empty calendar strip, and phone-width crop labels wrap correctly.

The Python endpoint retains its streamed 2 MB request cap, JSON/interface validation, fixed executable path, shell-free subprocess execution, two-process concurrency limit and 20-second execution timeout. Rust performs domain validation. The /docs workbench exposes the actual v0.2 interface.

Local validation (14 November 2026):
- Rust engine: 82 passed; native bridge: 5 passed.
- Python: 48 passed, one existing Starlette/AnyIO deprecation warning.
- Flutter full suite: 31 passed, two opt-in network tests skipped.
- Separate web_engine_test.dart with RUN_WEB_DEMO=true: all 5 passed, including live NASA -> Python HTTP -> actual Rust -> Flutter results widgets for January–December 2025.
- Flutter analysis: no errors/warnings; 24 informational Material-import deprecations.
- Flutter web release build passed. Current Wi-Fi host returned HTTP 200 and served JS identical to the rebuilt artifact.
- Real Rust HTTP result for the sample coordinates in 2025: 12 months, 365 days, 2280.56 mm rain, mean temperature 27.469178082191778 C.

Pending limits:
- Browser visual verification remains incomplete. Earlier in-app browser initialization timed out; Windows computer use stopped because it could not verify the browser URL. HTTP and widget checks are not claimed as visual browser verification.
- Ruff remains locally unverified after repeated dependency-download stalls. Exact blocker and Windows commands are in docs/WEB_DEMO.md.
- Verified agricultural recommendations and Android device validation remain separate future work.

Run ./Run-WebDemo.ps1; add -SkipBuild after building and -BindAddress 0.0.0.0 for local Wi-Fi testing. See docs/WEB_DEMO.md for verification commands and docs/OPENFARM_COMPARISON.md for the source-level comparison and missing-data scoring check. No OpenFarm implementation or unreviewed scoring thresholds were imported.

Keep this PR in draft. Do not merge into main.

sources.title: Harden NASA and Rust HTTP reliability with explicit integration diagnostics
sources.body:
NASA transport failures previously shared one code, queued climate/Rust requests could outlast client deadlines, and malformed Rust output or launch failures could escape as unstructured server errors. This change adds safe machine-readable errors, whole-operation deadlines, bounded Rust queueing, subprocess cleanup and response-envelope validation while preserving the climate, Rust integration and v0.2 payloads.

Opt-in POST diagnostics distinguish local health from uncached live NASA validation and real compiled Rust execution. They accept no user coordinates and return no climate payloads, secrets, paths or stack traces. Recent October 2026 NASA data returned GEOSIT; the existing MERRA-2 guard still rejects it. An exact real capture and source-verified versioned extension proposal are included for joint review; GEOS-IT is not enabled or relabeled.

Windows/Python 3.13, ports 8000/8080, same-origin Wi-Fi, proxy routing, adb reverse and diagnostic commands are documented in `server/docs/WINDOWS_RUNBOOK.md`. The request trace and local test evidence are in `server/docs/RELIABILITY_VERIFICATION.md`. No dashboard, crop algorithm, image-processing or Flutter policy changes.

Validation:
- Initial regression cases on the baseline: 9 failed, 2 passed; all now pass.
- Local Linux Python 3.12.14: 74 backend tests passed; Python 3.13.18 with the pinned lock: 74 passed, neither run skipped tests.
- Compiled Rust suite: 82 passed; Ruff, dependency compatibility and patch integrity passed.
- Actual HTTP on 8000/8080: live NASA → validation → compiled Rust, captured-real replay through Rust, cache miss/hit, unsupported GEOSIT rejection, localhost and direct host-address checks passed.
- Independent mocks cover transport/timeout failures, missing coverage, invalid metadata, process failure and malformed output. No fallback fixtures after errors.
- [Backend CI run 43580387304](https://github.com/SkyRR23/EarthSync/actions/runs/43580387304) passed all four Windows/Linux × Python 3.12/3.13 jobs at f28d2a3, including pinned installation, compiled Rust executable, Ruff and backend contract tests. Rust engine CI also passed. This completed after the local verification document was committed; it supplies the Windows CI evidence that document leaves pending.

Not verified: interactive Windows runbook/PowerShell hosting, physical Wi-Fi, Flutter browser/mock UI or Android device/FFI/USB flows; those tools/devices were unavailable locally. Same-host network-address checks do not prove separate-device LAN connectivity. Scientific/agronomic validation is not claimed.

Base: freshly fetched `feat/web-demo` at `e0cdaaf875efb376e3081a66826b4b5e21601c67`; isolated worktree and branch `fix/api-reliability-v2`.

sources.title: Milestone 7A: global onboarding and area/farm dashboards
sources.body:
New users previously had to select a field and enter the questionnaire before seeing data. This adds a global home dashboard with optional device/manual area selection or skipping, and a separate, explicit farm-point confirmation flow. Area changes never move a saved farm. Choices and confirmed farm records restore locally.

The dashboard presents existing NASA POWER monthly point-query climate and dated NASA GIBS imagery, with source/quality/missing-data labels. It performs no polygon averaging or crop analysis and never substitutes synthetic climate. Confirmed farms can open the existing questionnaire and detailed analysis. Native engine loading is deferred until analysis. Python/Rust contracts and agricultural calculations are unchanged.

Targets **feat/web-demo**, based on `e0cdaaf`; no existing PRs merged or branches replaced. Architecture, privacy notes, and exact Windows/web/Android commands: [docs/MILESTONE_7A.md](https://github.com/SkyRR23/EarthSync/blob/feat/global-onboarding-dashboard/docs/MILESTONE_7A.md).

Validation:
- 28 changed Dart files formatted; diff whitespace check passed.
- Flutter analysis passed with `--no-fatal-infos`: no errors/warnings, 32 informational Material-import deprecations.
- Flutter: **52 passed**, two opt-in network tests skipped; includes actual native bridge and all requested onboarding/state/outage cases.
- Rust engine **82 passed**; native bridge **5 passed**, release library built. Python **48 passed** including real Rust contract checks.
- Flutter release web build passed. **Actual desktop Chromium visual testing succeeded**, including live Nairobi climate graphs/provenance, dated satellite imagery, skip/manual area flow, confirmed farm/name, restore on refresh and questionnaire access.
- Phone-width widget tests passed. Mobile browser emulation was blocked by managed DevTools policy. Android APK/device testing remains outstanding because no Android SDK or phone is available here.

Draft for review; do not merge automatically. No photo recognition, SAR, chatbot, boundaries, or new crop suitability rules are included.

sources.title: Add evidence-grounded farmer assistant and reusable Flutter chat
sources.body:
## Behavior
Farmers can ask about rainfall, regional conditions, unavailable soil data, satellite evidence, crop findings and next inputs. Answers use deterministic retrieval and curated English/Spanish explanations, with citations and optional source details. Missing, contradictory, synthetic, stale or geographically ambiguous evidence stays unresolved. Supplied Rust decisions remain unchanged; no crop rankings, diagnoses, favorable forecasts or invented measurements are generated.

## Implementation
- Opt-in `assistant.v1-proposal` typed context/response boundary, generated JSON schemas and shared Python/Dart fixtures. Existing NASA and Rust v0.2 interfaces are unchanged.
- Stateless FastAPI router and standalone service; typed Flutter adapter with location/provenance binding; reusable chat screen/component with loading, retry, sources and protection against old-context replies.
- Standalone `app/lib/assistant_demo.dart`. No shared onboarding/navigation, app state providers, results screens or engine files edited. Integration and exact run/test commands: [docs/assistant/README.md](https://github.com/SkyRR23/EarthSync/blob/feat/farmer-assistant/docs/assistant/README.md).
- No model, API key, model download, provider fetch, autonomous action or persistent chat storage is needed. Approximate user location, selected region, confirmed farm and optional photo metadata remain separate.

## Validation
Local:
- 92 backend tests passed, including 44 assistant tests and existing Python/Rust contract checks.
- Actual Rust web executable built with `cargo build --locked --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --example web_engine`.
- New assistant Ruff checks/format and `git diff --check` passed.
- A real HTTP POST to the standalone service on port 8017 exactly matched the shared response fixture; missing rainfall remained null.

[Focused assistant CI](https://github.com/SkyRR23/EarthSync/actions/runs/43581637772) passed backend checks, Flutter analysis, 18 Flutter tests and standalone web build. [Existing Flutter integration CI](https://github.com/SkyRR23/EarthSync/actions/runs/43581637747) passed native Rust bridge build, full Flutter analysis/tests and default web build. Flutter 3.50.0/Dart 3.12 compatibility is retained; existing Material-import deprecation infos remain informational. Formatting is checked without modifying files. Monthly normalized provider records remain retrieved facts; only Rust seasonal summaries carry calculation attribution.

Representative exact commands (portable setup is documented):
```
PYTHONPATH=server /workspace/.earthsync-python/bin/python -m pytest -q server/tests
/workspace/.earthsync-python/bin/ruff check server/earthsync/assistant server/tests/assistant
/workspace/.earthsync-python/bin/ruff format --check server/earthsync/assistant server/tests/assistant
# From app/ with Flutter installed:
dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib/features/assistant lib/assistant_demo.dart test/assistant
flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos lib/features/assistant lib/assistant_demo.dart test/assistant
flutter test test/assistant --reporter expanded
flutter build web --target lib/assistant_demo.dart --no-wasm-dry-run
```

## Remaining integration limits
[Existing Python CI](https://github.com/SkyRR23/EarthSync/actions/runs/43581637743) stops at a pre-existing formatting failure in `server/tests/test_web_demo.py`, which is byte-for-byte unchanged from the integration baseline. New assistant checks pass and the complete backend suite passes locally. Shared owner files were not reformatted.

Current Rust reference records have no original provider-URL field; links stay null and incomplete provenance is visibly flagged. The proposed assistant boundary needs integration-owner review; 7A owns shared screen routing and the backend owner can mount the opt-in router. Both standalone entrypoints are provided now. No interactive browser, Android, live API or scientific validation was performed; the optional live NASA smoke was skipped. Local Flutter installation was blocked by environment network policy, so Flutter verification ran in GitHub Actions. Global example coordinates impose no geographic restriction. This is a draft and must not merge automatically.

sources.title: data: add global pilot crop knowledge and source evidence
sources.body:
EarthSync needs traceable crop references before v0.3 can evaluate agricultural requirements. This adds an offline catalog covering Story County corn/soybean, Tribune dryland winter wheat/sorghum/fallow, Stuttgart flooded rice/irrigated soybean, and Riverina drill-sown irrigated rice. Unknown parameters remain null with reasons; every populated parameter links to a scoped claim and original institutional source.

- Seven crop profiles plus a separate fallow profile; 13 original sources. Iowa has a detailed parameter/source desk review. Other pilots retain reference-only coverage. No independent agronomist or field validation is claimed.
- JSON Schema proposal `earthsync.crop-knowledge.v1-proposal`, per-parameter units/review states, dated source extracts, spatial/temporal support, deterministic bundle/pilot fixtures and byte-count/SHA-256 audit.
- Working exact-scope offline lookup, bounded non-overwriting source-capture command, 39 offline tests and dedicated CI. Production backend, Rust, Flutter and v0.2 interfaces are unchanged.
- `data/crop-knowledge/v1/CONTRACT.md` requests 7E review of system IDs, source graph, review semantics, advisory calendars and soil-versus-air temperature. Contract acceptance is pending; no engine exporter is installed.

Validation on Python 3.12.14 / jsonschema 4.26.0 / Ruff 0.14.5:
```sh
python data/crop-knowledge/v1/tools/catalog.py check
python -m unittest discover -s data/crop-knowledge/v1/tests -v
/workspace/.earthsync-python/bin/ruff check data/crop-knowledge/v1/tools data/crop-knowledge/v1/tests
/workspace/.earthsync-python/bin/ruff format --check data/crop-knowledge/v1/tools data/crop-knowledge/v1/tests
git diff --check
```
All passed (39 tests). Actual CLI lookups returned the Iowa reference profile, unavailable evidence for an uncovered Myanmar scope, and a distinct fallow management profile with null crop ID; none authorized recommendations. Exact setup/rebuild/retrieval commands are in the pack README and VALIDATION.md.

Source access limit: the web research tool successfully exposed all 13 institutional sources. Direct HTTP ingestion separately failed for all 13 with proxy tunnel 403; exact unavailable receipts are committed. Stored excerpt/data hashes are explicitly not original-provider-response hashes. Full original-response snapshots remain unavailable; copyrighted articles/PDFs are not redistributed.

All profiles retain `recommendation_eligible: false`. Harvest dates, cultivar durations, air-temperature limits, soil-depth requirements and stage Kc remain unavailable. Iowa calendar dates are advisory, insurance dates are excluded, soil establishment guidance cannot become NASA monthly T2M limits, and no forecast, yield, suitability score or rotation benefit is invented. PR #11 research values are not reused or cleared.

Base: `feat/web-demo` at `e0cdaaf875efb376e3081a66826b4b5e21601c67`. Changes confined to `data/crop-knowledge/` and its dedicated CI workflow. Keep draft; no merge or auto-merge. No browser, Android, live environmental API or scientific field validation is claimed.

Final CI on commit `c4112d2d2b69590b8a1e4b8118567635f08a866f`: both push and pull-request evidence jobs passed, including all 39 tests, lint, formatting, artifact/checksum checks and patch integrity. [PR CI run](https://github.com/SkyRR23/EarthSync/actions/runs/43580954169). Draft status retained; no merge or auto-merge enabled.

sources.title: Add farm photo evidence slice and optical/SAR adapter contracts
sources.body:
Farmers can upload, view, replace and delete field-photo evidence in a separate private workspace, without treating photo pixels or optional EXIF GPS as a confirmed farm location. This adds a reusable Flutter component and standalone harness, plus conservative point/date/product/geometry/QA matching and a structured evidence timeline.

HLS and OPERA RTC-S1 adapters return explicit unavailable states. NASA's HLS tutorial and OPERA processor documentation were researched at pinned GitHub revisions; direct catalog/product access was blocked by the environment proxy, and no live pixels or Earthdata access were verified. No satellite measurements, confidence scores or agronomic conclusions are fabricated.

- Images are bounded by MIME/signature, decode, size, dimension and animation checks; metadata is stripped locally before upload and again on the server. Consented GPS and farmer reports remain separate from farm confirmation.
- The additive `evidence.v1` service uses authenticated, atomic SQLite storage and a mockable adapter contract. A shared synthetic response fixture is checked in Python and Flutter. No 7A onboarding/dashboard routes, NASA POWER, Rust, FRB or v0.2 interfaces change. Two pre-existing web-demo test assertions receive formatting-only line wrapping to satisfy backend CI.
- `docs/PHOTO_EVIDENCE_V1.md` contains the proposed cross-component contract, exact commands, workflows, provider research, limits and integration handoff. One token authorizes one isolated private workspace; production identity/farm ownership integration needs the corresponding owner's review.

Validation: 122 Python tests passed, 2 live-service tests skipped; existing web-demo tests ran after building the Rust executable. All backend Ruff and formatting checks passed. Actual local HTTP synthetic upload/image retrieval/hash/timeline/deletion smoke passed. GitHub Actions with Flutter 3.50.0 resolved the committed lockfile, passed component/contract tests and the full native-bridge suite, and built the web app and independent photo harness. Local Flutter execution remains unavailable because the SDK is absent and its download host is denied. Browser interaction, Android execution, live NASA satellite and scientific validation were not performed.

sources.title: feat(environment): add evidence API and explicit source availability (7C)
sources.body:
Environmental inputs need explicit provenance and missing-data semantics before they can be used alongside farm context. This adds a standalone `POST /api/environmental/v1/context` service with versioned evidence envelopes for representative area points and farmer-confirmed farm points. It reports source availability and reference observations without agricultural diagnoses.

The implementation includes SoilGrids unit/depth/quantile readers, opt-in soil and Open-Meteo transport probes, separate source caches and attempt budgets, bounded timeouts, response hashes, explicit partial/null/rejected states, and weather model/timezone/freshness checks. Separate NDVI, EVI and surface-temperature adapters return unavailable until matching QA and pixel/composite support are verified. The additive contract, source trace, exact verification commands and actual blocked-provider probe are documented under `server/docs/environmental/`.

**Release blockers:** no independently live-validated soil or weather response was obtained. ISRIC documents its REST service as paused; this environment's enforced outbound policy blocks ISRIC/Open-Meteo. Default adapters therefore return unavailable without scientific numbers. The generic weather endpoint also lacks the required verified run/issue identity. Numeric probe readers remain reference-only with `usable_for_analysis=false`; satellite numeric ingestion, terrain/water, boundary aggregation and field-photo evidence are deferred. This draft does not claim a complete live soil service.

Reviewed PR #11's audited manifest, quality report and adapter proposal at `a85e2dd48805a36faebfec93c6991d5babb1add2`. None of its archived forecasts, shifted climatology or MODIS numbers is used as production input. Existing POWER routes, Flutter/dashboard, Rust and v0.2 interfaces are unchanged.

Validation:
- 110 backend tests passed, including existing POWER replay, actual compiled Rust compatibility and 62 new environmental tests.
- Actual Uvicorn loopback health and context POST passed, including explicit unavailable envelopes and null diagnosis.
- Repository-wide Ruff lint, new-package/test formatting, dependency check and staged patch integrity passed.
- The full formatter check has a pre-existing failure in two assertions in `server/tests/test_web_demo.py`, reproduced directly from the untouched integration baseline; that file remains unchanged.
- The live provider probe exited 1 with transport-unavailable states; no browser, Android, live-source success, farm ground-truth or scientific validation is claimed.

Base: `feat/web-demo` at `e0cdaaf875efb376e3081a66826b4b5e21601c67`. Isolated branch/worktree: `feat/environmental-context-v1`, `/workspace/EarthSync-environmental-context`. Draft for integration and source-acceptance review; do not merge automatically.

sources.title: feat(engine): implement agricultural evidence engine v0.3
sources.body:
The existing engine cannot evaluate daily growing-period climate, numerical soil requirements, crop-stage ETc or sourced succession constraints. This adds an offline deterministic v0.3 evaluator and `analyze_v03_json` under the proposed `earthsync.engine.v0.3.0` contract. Existing v0.2, integration, Flutter, Python and NASA POWER interfaces remain unchanged.

Implemented behavior:
- Versioned crop identities and separate dryland, rainfed, irrigated and flooded-lowland profiles, with per-rule/source review, applicability, cultivar and evidence limitations.
- Daily temperature-range checks, explicitly sourced-base uncapped GDD, inclusive/cross-year growing periods, planting windows, duration and complete-period rainfall. Missing/suspect days, ambiguous series and historical/forecast/calendar mismatches remain explicit.
- Depth/method-aware pH, carbon, bulk-density and volumetric-moisture comparisons, supported unit conversions, categorical texture/drainage, and retained farmer/model contradictions.
- Optional aligned Kc × ET0 calculations and a separate flooded-management check. No inferred water balance, irrigation adequacy, default coefficients or wetness-to-moisture conversion.
- Ordered rotation and history overlap checks, crop/family succession rules, explicit fallow evidence, and unranked successor scenarios from approved applicable catalog entries.
- Five evidence/validation states, compact source-traceable Flutter summaries and separate detailed findings/full input context. No arbitrary scores, confidence percentages, yield claims or LLM dependency.

The runnable comprehensive fixture uses fictional crop identities and thresholds labeled synthetic. Synthetic evidence is restricted to software-test calculations and cannot produce real-world recommendations. Whole scenarios remain insufficient unless a supplied constraint conflicts; a finite list of passing rules does not establish complete suitability.

Contract, examples, formulas, evidence semantics and exact commands: [docs/ENGINE_CONTRACT_v0.3.md](docs/ENGINE_CONTRACT_v0.3.md). Minimal no-source/no-profile request/response fixtures verify the public JSON envelope.

Validation on Rust 1.99.0: 111 engine tests (82 existing + 29 v0.3), five existing bridge host tests, rustfmt, Clippy with warnings denied, offline JSON examples and patch integrity all passed:

```sh
cargo fmt --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml
cargo fmt --check --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml
cargo test --offline --locked --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml
cargo clippy --all-targets --offline --locked --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml -- -D warnings
cargo test --offline --locked --manifest-path app/rust/Cargo.toml
cargo run --offline --locked --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --example v03_demo
git diff --check
```

The first offline bridge attempt lacked flutter_rust_bridge; a locked dependency download/test succeeded, then offline host tests passed. FAO-56 equation 56 and FAO paddy scheduling guidance were inspected via web lookup; this validates the documented method references, not the synthetic coefficients or local agricultural applicability. Browser, Android, live NASA and scientific field validation were not run.

Cross-team contract review is pending:
- Crop catalog owner: agree versioned crop/profile IDs, family/cultivar, exact requirement statistics, per-rule sources/review and geographic/system applicability. No separate v0.3 catalog branch was advertised during inspection; no real thresholds are bundled or independently approved here.
- Environmental owners (#8, #11): agree daily calendar semantics, Tmax/Tmin coverage, fill/quality handling, parameter lineage/spatial support, soil validity/depth/method and reference-ET0 definition. The current backend's T2M/PRECTOTCORR monthly output cannot supply these new daily requirements. Research-pack records retain their existing reference/unavailable limitations.
- Flutter owner: adopt a new versioned wrapper/decoder only after agreement, retaining separate approximate user location, confirmed farm, photo metadata, nulls, order and all statuses.

New real-catalog/daily/soil/ET0 adapters remain unavailable pending reviewed records and schema agreement; no external responses are fabricated. This draft targets latest integration baseline `feat/web-demo` at `e0cdaaf875efb376e3081a66826b4b5e21601c67`, from the isolated `feat/agronomic-engine-v03` worktree. Do not merge automatically.
